## Receipt request through Nikolajew: the other p105 telegram

**Sources on this page:** p105 A. [Concise case study](../radio/nov2_nikolajew_acknowledgment.md).

<a id="edition-cases-radio-nov2-nikolajew-acknowledgment-receipt-request-through-nikolajew-the-other-p105-telegram"></a>



**Source review and edition: icekylinx and GPT-6 Astra Pro.**

This is the 300-slot **section A** on Childs p105, a request to confirm receipt of two communications to Mackensen command through Nikolajew. It is separate from the original [p105 challenge](#edition-cases-p105), which is the 290-slot section B. The complete native source yields 150 fixed output labels without changing any coordinate or square cell.


**Reviewed source crops:** [p105_reviewed.png](../../experiments/nov2_nikolajew_acknowledgment/sources/p105_reviewed.png). [File and pixel verification](../../sources/reviewed-crops.md#verify).

### p105 A

**Source transcription — header:** `A) FUER UKS v LP (5.10 p.m., November 2nd); 1530 (2/11); RICHI-300`

<details>
<summary>Raw decoded text</summary>

**Raw output — every native source slot in printed order:**

```text
ANXOBERKDOXMACKENSENXEMPFANGSBESTAETIGUNGXVONXRMX1XAXA1118XGEHXOPXUNDXRMX1XAX111M7XGEHXOPXUEBERXNIKOLAJEWXDURCHXFTXERBETENXOHLXRMX1XAXNOX104716XGEWXOP
```

</details>

**Readable German — the same nonseparator labels as the unchanged raw output:**

> An Oberkdo. Mackensen. Empfangsbestaetigung von RM. 1. A. A1118 GEH. OP. und RM. 1. A. 111M7 GEH. OP. ueber Nikolajew durch F. T. erbeten. OHL. RM. 1. A. No. 104716 GEW. OP.

**Meaning:** The message requests radio confirmation through Nikolajew that Mackensen command received the two referenced communications. The raw reference strings A1118 and 111M7, and the final GEW designation, are preserved.

<a id="edition-cases-radio-nov2-nikolajew-acknowledgment-editorial-limits"></a>

#### Editorial limits

- This physical record is section A; the original p105 challenge concerns the different 290-slot section B and retains its identifier and earlier attribution.
- All 300 source slots are retained in the printed order. The earlier 308-slot OCR block included seven characters from the next header and expanded printed DXXXX to six characters; correcting the machine transcription is not an alteration of the historical ciphertext.
- The primary readable display changes spacing and punctuation only. A1118, 111M7 and GEW are not silently converted to more familiar references.
- A separately priced interpretation compares the two references with independent p105 C1 and p106 A2; agreement of subject matter supports a reference-identification hypothesis, not an assertion that the telegrams are identical copies.

<a id="edition-cases-radio-nov2-nikolajew-acknowledgment-conditional-interpretation-of-the-reference-fields"></a>

### Conditional interpretation of the reference fields

The different telegram on [p105 C1](#edition-cases-radio-nov2-telegram-acknowledgments-p105-c1) addresses A. O. K. Mackensen and prints `11118` and `11127` together in a request to acknowledge receipt. Its continuation [p106 A2](#edition-cases-radio-nov2-telegram-acknowledgments-p106-a2) again uses `11127`. Those native readings supply a concrete comparison for this section A’s `A1118` and `111M7`.

Identifying the communications mentioned here with that independently received reference pair is an **additional assumption**. The texts have different wording and their own outgoing references. Topic, addressee and date proximity do not prove that their serials must be identical. The native p105 A fields stay unchanged above.

| Proposed change | Extra observed-coordinate substitution | Source index, zero-based |
| --- | ---: | --- |
| `A1118` → `11118` | 1 | 194: `G` → `F` |
| `111M7` → `11127` | 1 | 260: `V` → `F` |
| Final `GEW` → `GEH` | 1 | 94: `G` → `V` |

The first two changes together cost **two substitutions**. The final abbreviation normalization is a separate, third substitution; the reference comparison does not authenticate that footer correction.

**Conditional interpretation — both reference identifications, two substitutions in total:**

```text
ANXOBERKDOXMACKENSENXEMPFANGSBESTAETIGUNGXVONXRMX1XAX11118XGEHXOPXUNDXRMX1XAX11127XGEHXOPXUEBERXNIKOLAJEWXDURCHXFTXERBETENXOHLXRMX1XAXNOX104716XGEWXOP
```

**Conditional interpretation — both references plus the separate footer normalization, three substitutions in total:**

```text
ANXOBERKDOXMACKENSENXEMPFANGSBESTAETIGUNGXVONXRMX1XAX11118XGEHXOPXUNDXRMX1XAX11127XGEHXOPXUEBERXNIKOLAJEWXDURCHXFTXERBETENXOHLXRMX1XAXNOX104716XGEHXOP
```

The verifier independently decodes the cited native records, checks their unchanged key and exact reference positions, and re-encrypts both optional p105 A streams. These alternatives count as no additional physical record and do not enter the primary zero-repair totals.

<a id="edition-cases-radio-nov2-nikolajew-acknowledgment-reproduction-and-credit"></a>

### Reproduction and credit

Run `python experiments/nov2_nikolajew_acknowledgment/verify.py --verify`. Add `--pdf /path/to/adfgvx-childs.pdf` to check the original PDF and the exact rendered pixels of the preserved source excerpt.

The verifier reconstructs source-coordinate pairs, checks raw domains, replays all priced changes, verifies the readable display without dropping unresolved labels, and checks a global completion witness where required. Such a completion is mechanical evidence, not a historical guess.

Published period keys: George Lasry, Ingo Niebel, Nils Kopal and Arno Wacker (2016), and George Lasry (2017 key list). Earlier repository OCR and unchanged-key outputs are retained separately. Source review and explicit editorial work: icekylinx and GPT-6 Astra Pro.

## p105 — Naval telegram acknowledgments

**Sources on this page:** p105. [Concise case study](../p105.md).

<a id="edition-cases-p105-p105--naval-telegram-acknowledgments"></a>



**Status:** Earlier raw body reproduced exactly; repaired stream still has an unpaired coordinate. **Key:** `Nov1-3`.

**Earliest credited record:** [Norbert, 2017-03-01, comment 15](https://scienceblogs.de/klausis-krypto-kolumne/2017/02/23/the-top-50-unsolved-encrypted-messages-46-unsolved-adfgvx-cryptograms-from-world-war-1/?all=1#comment-852622). **Current source and arithmetic review:** icekylinx and GPT-6 Astra Pro, 2 November 2026.

<a id="edition-cases-p105-most-likely-reading"></a>

### Most likely reading

**Readable German — earlier credited reconstruction, with unresolved fields retained:**

> Germania-[Etappe] Konstantinopel. Fuer [Mittelmeerdivision]. Zu [Tel. Nr.] 62, [Div.-Telegr. Nr.] 58: […] 32141 Q4 A vom 4. November [erledigt]. [Admiralstab]. 32398 B.

**Meaning:** A message for the Mediterranean naval division, routed through the Germania staging organization in Constantinople, reports that a matter in earlier telegrams has been dealt with. The intervening reference wording is damaged.

**Notes:** Brackets mark editorial interpretations of garbled words. The reference numbers are retained without attempting to reconstruct their administrative meaning. Baertl's longer completion is printed below for attribution; its extra wording is not recovered by the 143-position model. The final unpaired coordinate and its optional deletion are separately certified.

<a id="edition-cases-p105-explicit-repair-of-the-orphan-coordinate"></a>

### Explicit repair of the orphan coordinate

The unpaired final intermediate `D` comes from original source index **244** (the 245th received character, final `D` of group 49 `XAXGD`). Deleting it in addition to the three published deletions produces 286 coordinates and exactly the same 143-position body, now with a complete ordinary re-encryption. This equivalent reconstruction is a contribution of the present arithmetic review; it does not establish the historical error mechanism.

A separate [optional two-deletion model](../../experiments/p105_optional_two_deletions/README.md) retains 288 of the 290 printed coordinates and gives a fully paired 144-label raw stream, with three explicitly priced ordinary-word substitutions. It preserves the earlier reading above and documents all twelve equal-cost word-only deletion descriptions, retrospective held-out comparisons and independent native vocabulary witnesses. Its changed reference/date labels remain geometry-dependent alternatives, and the visibly printed excluded coordinates remain in its full source ledger.

<a id="edition-cases-radio-nov2-telegram-acknowledgments-earlier-page-third-part-witness"></a>

#### Earlier-page third-part witness

The p104 source says that parts 1 and 2 are missing and dates its message `1/11`; the three-part copy is dated `2/11`. The p104 body differs from p106 A3 in exactly **source coordinate 54**, V versus X. That changes **plaintext position 68** from 3 to 6: `104359` versus `104659`. Both sources are kept unchanged. The shared wording supports a near-copy relationship, not permission to overwrite either date or reference.
